extracted.intended_audience: citizens, delegates, and framers considering constitutional design and the ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and principles for structuring a republican government to prevent concentration of power: separation of departments, checks and balances, appointment and financial independence, federal subdivision, and rules for representative qualifications and elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of the three departments (legislative, executive, judiciary)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the powers of government, legislative, executive, and judiciary, result to the legislative body. The legislative, executive, and judiciary departments should be separate and distinct, so that no person should exercise the powers of more than one of them at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely writing a demarcation on parchment is insufficient; there must be practical barriers so that no person exercises more than one department's powers. Examples: warning against 'elective despotism' and reference to abuses in various States where legislative powers swallowed executive and judicial functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentration of powers / prevent elective despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: The concentrating [of powers] in the same hands is precisely the definition of despotic government. An ELECTIVE DESPOTISM was not the government we fought for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if powers are exercised by many persons, a concentration may be equally oppressive ('One hundred and seventy-three despots would surely be as oppressive as one'). The constitution must divide and balance powers among several bodies so no one can transcend legal limits without effective checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional recourse to the people (occasional appeals/conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (from Notes on the State of Virginia): whenever any two of the three branches concur (each by two-thirds) that a convention is necessary for altering or correcting breaches of the constitution, a convention shall be called.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While appealing to the people respects the original fountain of power, objections include: it fails if two departments combine against the third; frequent appeals would erode reverence for government and stability; public passions and party spirit would often decide questions rather than reason; the legislature enjoys decisive advantages (numbers, local influence) that bias outcomes. The convention would often be composed of persons connected to the very department under scrutiny, risking partiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodical appeals / censures (fixed-interval revisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodical appeals to the people (at fixed periods) have been proposed as a means to prevent and correct infractions of the constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms: if intervals are short, reviews reflect recent passions; if distant, abuses remain long unremedied and become entrenched; a distant censorial review is a weak restraint on present excesses; practical example: Pennsylvania's Council of Censors showed party split, partiality, questionable decisions, and inefficacy—sometimes contemporary legislatures ignored the council's constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior structure: mutual checks through institutional design
rubrics_metrics.description: As exterior provisions are inadequate, supply the defect by contriving the interior structure so constituent parts, by their mutual relations, keep each other in their proper places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each department should have a will of its own; the government must be arranged so different offices are checks on one another and private interest is a sentinel over public rights. 'Ambition must be made to counteract ambition.' Provide constitutional means and personal motives for each department to resist encroachments of the others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment independence between departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each department should have as little agency as possible in the appointment of the members of the others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally all supreme appointments would derive independently from the people through separate channels; practical deviations are admitted, especially for the judiciary where qualifications and permanence matter. The goal is to prevent appointment-based dependence that could erode departmental independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial/emolument independence of officeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each department should be as little dependent as possible on those of the others for the emoluments annexed to their offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, for example, the executive or judges are dependent on the legislature for salaries or emoluments, their independence in other respects would be nominal. Example: the constitution requires judges' salaries to be fixed; varying them undermines judicial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent legislative usurpation of executive and judicial functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislature has means to assume executive and judiciary powers; in many instances it has decided rights which should have been left to judicial controversy, and the direction of the executive during sessions is becoming habitual and familiar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against laws that draw judiciary cases into legislative cognizance, alter judges' salaries, or otherwise usurp functions; printing of bills and other constitutional precautions exist to check improper legislative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide the legislature into distinct branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the legislative authority necessarily predominates in a republic, the remedy is to divide the legislature into different branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the branches different by modes of election and principles of action so they are as little connected as their common functions will admit. This reduces the danger of legislative aggrandizement at the expense of other departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortify the executive relative to the legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: The weakness of the executive may require that it should be fortified; an absolute negative (veto) appears a natural defense but may be unsafe or insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider qualified connections between the executive and a weaker branch of the legislature so that the latter may support the constitutional rights of the former without being too detached from its own departmental rights. Be cautious: an absolute negative might be perfidiously abused or not exerted when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of federal (compound) structure as double security
rubrics_metrics.description: In the compound republic of America, the power surrendered by the people is divided between two distinct governments, and then subdivided among departments — yielding a double security to the rights of the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different governments will control each other and each will be controlled internally. The federal principle disperses interests and classes so oppressive combinations of a majority of the whole are less likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity of interests and sects to protect minority rights
rubrics_metrics.description: In a free government the security for civil rights consists in the multiplicity of interests; for religious rights in the multiplicity of sects. The degree of security depends on the number of interests and sects, which in turn depends on the extent of country and number of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehending many separate descriptions of citizens makes unjust combinations of a majority improbable. Larger extended republics can better secure self-government and minority rights than small, narrow polities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for Representatives and terms to ensure dependence on the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative qualifications: age 25; seven years a citizen; inhabitant of the State at election; during service be in no office under the United States. Elections: biennial elections secure immediate dependence and sympathy with the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elector qualifications are to conform to State standards for the most numerous branch of State legislatures. Biennial elections are recommended because frequent elections keep the branch intimately connected with public opinion, but the precise interval depends on circumstances and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity of proposed laws (printing bills prior to consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requiring that all bills of a public nature shall be previously printed for the consideration of the people is one of the constitutional precautions against improper acts of legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to print bills was cited as an instance of constitutional violation in Pennsylvania; printing is relied on by the constitution to prevent hasty or improper legislative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve constitutional trial by jury
rubrics_metrics.description: The constitutional trial by jury had been violated in some instances; such rights belong to the judiciary and should not be assumed by the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative encroachment on jury trial and judicial functions undermines the separation of powers; these matters should be left to judicial controversy unless constitutionally altered.
